notes: HVS1, HVS2, HVS3, HVS4, HVS5, HVS6, and HVS7 are the unbound HVSs identified or used by this paper; HVS1-HVS3 are prior discoveries not from this survey (T:p6-b7), while HVS4-HVS7 are the previously discovered survey HVSs explicitly covered by the range at T:p3-b12 and individually labeled at I:p3-b8. The 11 Table 1 objects, including SDSS J144955.58+310351.4, are described as possible bound HVSs (T:p5-b6; I:p5-b6), so they are not included as Galactic-unbound candidates. The paper reports no new unbound HVS (T:p7-b3); Table 2 is described as online-only and is not supplied (T:p8-b45).

HVS1: Target star HVS1 is the first HVS discovered (Brown et al. 2005a), identified in this paper as the highest-significance positive-velocity outlier (e.g., T:p3-b12). The quoted Galactic rest-frame velocity is explicitly a minimum ("at least +709 ± 12 km s-1"); this is recorded as a lower bound, and the ±12 km/s uncertainty is noted here because the schema does not permit an error together with a bound. No individual right ascension, declination, parallax, proper motion, Galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS1 in the supplied material. The predicted proper motions of 0.5–1 mas/yr in T:p7-b19 refer to the HVS sample generally, not to HVS1 specifically, so they are not recorded.

HVS2: HVS2 is only mentioned in T:p5-b5 as an 8 M⊙ HVS discussed in connection with a possible blue-straggler origin, and in T:p6-b7 as one of the unbound HVSs not from this survey located in the anti-center hemisphere 90 < l < 270 deg. The paper reports no numerical values for HVS2 for any of the requested quantities, so none were extracted.

HVS3: The identifier HVS3 corresponds to the literature hypervelocity star of Hirsch et al. (2005), which this paper mentions only once, in §4 (T:p6-b7): "the 3 unbound HVSs not from this survey, HVS1 (Brown et al. 2005a), HVS2 (Edelmann et al. 2005), and HVS3 (Hirsch et al. 2005), are also located in the anti-center hemisphere 90 < l < 270°." No equatorial coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS3 anywhere in the supplied text, tables (Table 1 lists only the survey's possible bound HVSs by SDSS designation), or figures (Figure 5 marks only HVS1 plus this survey's stars). The only stated property is its location in the Galactic hemisphere 90° < l < 270°, which is a general Galactic-longitude range rather than a reported equatorial position or velocity, so no eligible quantity is extracted. (Note: HVS3 should not be confused with the third row of Table 1, SDSS J075712.93+512938.0, which is not labeled HVS3 in the paper.)

HVS4: The paper refers to HVS4 only as one of the four previously discovered unbound HVSs (HVS4–HVS7; see T:p3-b12, T:p4-b6, and T:p6-b5). It does not report individual coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS4. Table 1 (T:p5-b6, I:p5-b6) lists 11 possible bound HVSs but does not include HVS4. HVS4 is plotted collectively with other HVSs in Figures 3–5, but no numeric values are tabulated for it in the supplied material, so no quantities were extracted.

HVS5: HVS5 is identified only as one of the previously discovered HVSs (HVS4-HVS7) in T:p3-b12. The supplied Figure 3 (I:p3-b8) labels HVS5 with a vertical marker but provides no tabulated numeric value, coordinates, distance, or probability for HVS5. The online data table (Table 2) that might contain its coordinates and heliocentric velocity is not included in the supplied material. Therefore no quantity for HVS5 can be extracted without adding unsupported or inferred values.

HVS6: The target star HVS6 appears in the text only as a member of the "four HVSs previously discovered in this survey (HVS4 - HVS7)" (T:p3-b12) that are unbound HVSs. This paper reports no individual quantities (coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability) for HVS6 itself. Table 1 (T:p5-b6) lists only possible bound HVS candidates, and Table 2 (the on-line data table) lists new survey observations; neither provides values specifically for HVS6. No numerical values can therefore be extracted for this star.

HVS7: The target star HVS7 is mentioned only as one of the four previously discovered unbound HVSs (HVS4-HVS7) from this survey (T:p3-b12), with no individually reported coordinates, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS7 in the supplied text, figures, or tables. The paper states that these four HVS discoveries are published elsewhere (Brown et al. 2006a,b), and the online data table (Table 2) is not included in the supplied materials. Therefore no quantities can be extracted for HVS7.
